elements.evidence: The grant expressly extends to “Customer, its Affiliates” and defines Affiliates; the third-party-access carveout confirms their permitted use.

elements.element: Licence covers contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “contractors acting on Customer's behalf,” and states that their access is not prohibited third-party access.
The licence ends upon expiration or termination of the Agreement and is not stated to be perpetual. Although it is royalty-free, the clause does not establish that paid-up licences are absent.
The licence remains revocable upon expiration or termination under Section 4 and is not expressly irrevocable. The clause does not establish that paid-up licences are absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: The licence may end upon expiration or any termination permitted under Section 4, rather than solely for material breach. The clause does not establish that subscription licences are absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if the breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no uncured-breach requirement or cure condition and instead incorporates all expiration and termination rights under Section 4.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The licence is transferable in connection with an assignment permitted under the Agreement, and Section (h) permits assignment to asset purchasers and successors through merger, stock sale, consolidation, or similar transactions.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered by the licence.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are direct licensees under the express grant.

elements.element: Affiliate coverage requires no more than written notice from Customer to Kubient.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants affiliate coverage automatically, without requiring notice, consent, or an amendment; this is more favorable than coverage conditioned only on written notice.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The licence permits transfer with an assignment allowed under Section (h), which expressly permits assignment to a successor by merger, stock sale, consolidation, or similar transaction without consent.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the fallback and adds the requested affiliate and contractor coverage, but it does not make paid-up licences perpetual or irrevocable and does not restrict subscription termination to uncured material breach. It is not minimal to the completed fallback because it also changes contractor access and revocability and adds a new responsibility for affiliate and contractor compliance. The express third-party-access carveout avoids conflict with subsection (a), and unrelated terms remain operative.
